install.label: 03 / installation
install.heading: How to install
install.description: Four steps. A clean, dry surface gives the strongest bond.
install.image_12_alt: Steps 1 and 2: remove the old skates and clean the base
install.image_34_alt: Steps 3 and 4: align the dots and press them in place
install.step_1_text: Carefully remove all existing skates, including any double-sided adhesive. Make sure no residue is left behind.
install.step_2_text: Wipe each skate slot with the alcohol pad to remove dust, oils or adhesive residue. Let it dry completely.
install.step_3_text: Choose the right size dot. Align each dot with the edge of the mouse for balance and stability.
install.step_4_text: Once all dots are in place, press firmly on each one for a few seconds to make sure it bonds.

faq.label: 04 / FAQ
faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Yes. {{ name }} dots are universal, so they fit any mouse. Place them where the original skates sat, keep them clear of the sensor opening and spread them evenly so the mouse sits flat.
faq.q2: How many dots should I use?
faq.a2: Start with one of the recommended layouts. Fewer dots give a faster, lighter glide; more dots add contact and control. Adjust until it feels right.
faq.q3: Do I need to remove my original skates?
faq.a3: Yes. Remove the original skates and any leftover adhesive first, then clean the base with the included prep pad and let it dry completely.
faq.q4: Which mousepads does {{ name }} work on?
faq.a4: {{ name }} is made for both cloth and glass mousepads.
faq.q5: What is the difference between Ice Version and Control Version?
faq.a5: Ice Version is our speed skate, for a fast, low-friction glide. Control Version is our control skate, with more stopping power for precise, controlled aim.
faq.q6: Will the dots change how my mouse tracks?
faq.a6: Not when they are applied evenly. Dots that sit level keep the sensor at a consistent height, so tracking stays reliable. If the mouse rocks, adjust or add a dot until it sits flat.

about.label: About us
about.heading: rawdot
about.quote: “rawdot began from a practical problem: replacing worn mouse skates in Mexico was often more complicated than the product itself.”
about.description: Gaming mice can last for years while their original skates gradually wear down. Universal dots became a more flexible alternative—one created from the perspective of a gamer in Mexico.
about.value_1_text: rawdot grew out of a real, local problem: good replacement skates were hard to find.
about.value_2_text: We design what we want to use ourselves, from first-hand experience.
about.value_3_text: Simple products, clear packaging and instructions you can actually follow.
about.value_4_text: Skates first, with glasspads and arm sleeves on the way.
